```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(lubridate)
library(svglite)
library(kableExtra)
library(showtext)

setwd(here::here())

#font_add_google("IBM Plex Sans", "ibm")
extrafont::loadfonts()
week_sel=8

pretty_table <- function(x){
  kable(x) %>%
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover"),
      full_width = FALSE,
      position = "left"
    )
}

source("scripts/league_data.R")
```

[See all the recaps for the 2026 season](https://jshannon75.github.io/pcfl/)

## Week `r week_sel` Headlines

* The Captain capsizes!
* The Sharks continue their offensive blitz
* Pigskin on the Gridiron getting hot
* Pigskin vs the Captain: this week's prime matchup

## Last week's games

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(lastweek_results)
```

And then there were none. The headline story this week is that Captain Clairvoyant was the last unbeaten team...until they faced the Georgia Peanuts! My scrappy upstarts managed to pull off the upset.

In other games, the Henry's had an impressive week, but not as much as the Southern Sharks. Sarah's team now has the top three scoring performances in league history.

## Best performances

### Best players overall
Here's last week's **10 best performing players.** 

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(top_n(starters,10,Points) %>%
        arrange(-Points))
```

It's not often that tight ends make this list, but Brock Bowers is special.  Also, Bhayshul Tuten is a great name.

### Best bench
Who won the **best scoring bench** award last week?

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(starter_benchteam %>% 
        arrange(-`Bench points`) %>%
  rename(Team=`PCFL Team`))
```

#### Season bench standings

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
pretty_table(starter_benchteam_all %>%
         arrange(-`Bench points`) %>%
 rename(Team=name))
```

The Hobbits take the lead in the all-important bench standings!

### Waiver masters

I've tallied the players picked up by each team since the draft and the points they've contributed as starters. Here's where those stand.

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(roster_pickup %>%
        select(-abbrev) %>%
        rename(Team=name,Points=draftpoints,
               Transactions=draft_num) %>%
        arrange(-Points)) 
```

### Recapping the draft
Here's the amount of points drafted players have contributed to each team as starters.

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(roster_draft %>% 
         select(-abbrev) %>%
        rename(Team=name,Points=draftpoints) %>% 
        arrange(-Points))
```

No surprise that our top teams are those that drafted best--Sarah and Ted/Elaine had a good draft night.

### Best team performances 

Here's a list of the **top five scoring performances** so far this season.

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(toppoints %>%
        arrange(-Score))
```

Both Sarah and Ted/Elaine jumped on the list this week. And those two weeks at 190+ points are 2 and 3 in league history. The Sharks are doing very, very, VERY well.

## Looking ahead

### League standings

Our league standings are a little unusual. We rank teams based on points, kinda like hockey. There are two ways to get points:

* Win your weekly matchup (1 point)
* Finish in the top six point scorers (1 point)

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(standings)
```

Sarah and the Sharks are now our league leaders, with the Henry's and Captain close behind. Richard is lurking behind Evan for that last playoff spot.

### Playoff Odds

I've created 10,000 simulations of the remaining matchups based on teams' performances so far. Here's what playoff odds look like based on those results:

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(playoff_odds %>%
  mutate(
    Odds      = scales::percent(PlayoffOdds, accuracy = 0.1),
    TopSeed   = scales::percent(TopSeed, accuracy = 0.1),
    AvgSeed   = round(AvgSeed, 2),
    ExpPoints = round(ExpPoints, 1)
  ) %>%
  select(Team = name, Odds, TopSeed, AvgSeed, ExpPoints))
```

The algorithm still really likes those top 4.

```{r}
#| echo: false
pretty_table(nextwk1)
```

Classic rivalry: Richard (Pigskin) vs. Brian (Captain). They have a long history, and so there's no surprises. May the best team win.
